To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the facets and aspects of Big Five personality are associated with affective disorder.

most facets of neurotic personality are positively associated with affectives disorders, positive emotion in extroverted personality, and competence and conscientiousness are negatively associated with affectives disorder, and trust in agreeable personality and actions in open personality are negatively associated with anxiety disorder, and fantasy in open personality is positively associated with anxiety disorder.
neuroticism, positive affect, competence, self-discipline and trust correlate with various anxiety disorders, whereas withdrawal and industriousness are associated with depressive disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association between personality and mental disorders.
the relationship between personality traits and affective disorders.
the relationship between affective disorders, personality traits, and lower order personality constructs, such as personality facets and aspects
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the facets of neurotic personality, namely anxiety, depression, self consciousness, impulsiveness, vulnerability, and angry hostility, are associated with anxiety disorders and depressive disorders.
neuroticism is a risk factor for affective disorders, conscientiousness is protective, and extroversion is protective for depressive disorders.
personality facets are associated with affective disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Big Five personality facets and aspects can be used as a tool in the diagnosis of affective disorders.

personality facets and aspects can help to understand affective disorders, but further research is needed to understand the direction of the relationship between personality and affective disorders, and the mechanisms underlying these relationships
neuroticism, positive emotions and conscientiousness are important for understanding affective disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Big Five personality facets are associated with affective disorder, and that these associations are not always consistent with the Big Five domains.
the lower order facets of personality may be better predictors of affective disorders than the higher order traits.
personality traits are important in the aetiology of depression and anxiety disorders.
